To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the successful synthesis of HA, β-TCP and BCPs of the two was obtained by means of wet chemical precipitation, and that the resulting crystals were characterized.
the curcumin loaded synthetic ceramics were found to increase MG-63 cells alkaline phosphatases, which suggests that these materials could be useful in bone remodeling.
the curcumin loaded BCPs showed a better performance than the pure HA and TCP particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of HA, TCP and BCP, the curcumin loading, and release of the curcumin and the in vitro studies with osteoblast-like MG-63 cells.
the synthesis of hydroxy-apatite, β-TCP and two BCPs of the two, and their use for the delivery of curcumin to bone cells.
the development of new biomaterials for bone tissue engineering, which can act as carriers of bioactive agents, such as curcumin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BCPs are promising carriers of curcumin for local treatment in the field of bone tissue engineering.
the curcumin release is directly proportional to the TCP phase content in the biphasic ceramic, and that this is a promising approach for the development of curcumin-based bone grafts.
the synthesis of curcumin loaded BCPs is feasible, and the results are promising for further in vitro and in vivo studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new method for the synthesis of hydroxyapatiite, β-tricalcium phosphate and biphasic calcium phosphate (BCP), and that the BCP can be loaded with curcumin, which is released in a controlled fashion and does not cause any cytotoxicity.
curcumin-loaded biphasic calcium phosphates (BCP) particles are a promising candidate to act as local delivery carriers of curcumin in bone regeneration applications.
we have developed a novel and promising approach for the use of a curcumin-loaded ceramic for the treatment of bone diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the curcumin release profile can be tuned to a large extent by controlling the ceramic composition and the curcumin concentration in solution.
curcumin-loaded BCP particles can be used to promote the differentiation of osteogenic cells.
the synthesis of BCPs is a feasible route to obtain curcumin-loaded particles for the treatment of bone diseases.
